objective: Test one segment-aware router that classifies existing acquisition metadata as metadata and uses an order-sensitive text encoder to select the capability-bearing segment, without adding teacher outputs or changing LayerCake.
causal_basis: V43 passed aggregate body routing at 95.36% but failed unchanged original prompts at 38.14%, isolating whole-prompt header entanglement. Its weakest body capabilities also show that mean pooling discards useful order. V44 changes both measured mechanisms and does not tune V43 steps, seed, labels, or tokenizer.

segmentation.rule: When a prompt contains multiple lines, classify the first line and the unchanged remaining text as separate semantic segments; otherwise classify the entire prompt as one segment.
segmentation.selection: Exclude segments predicted as metadata, then select the remaining segment with the greatest capability probability. If every segment is predicted metadata, fail-soft to the segment with the greatest capability probability.

supervision.capability_view: unchanged acquisition body with its existing Phase 1 capability label
supervision.metadata_view: unchanged acquisition first line with a metadata label derived only from the pre-existing prompt boundary

decision_rule: Run only R0 seed 240044. A full pass of aggregate original, aggregate body, every original-prompt capability, and metadata rejection may authorize exactly two locked replication seeds. Any miss closes V44 and prohibits replications and a routed LayerCake host.
claim_boundary: Standalone ABI router gate only; not English generation, Phase 3 certification, LayerCake quality, or ABI superiority.
